lines.text: Rahul has six projects and one resume line: worked on an AI chatbot. In placement season, that line gets a quick skim and nothing more.
The fix isn't a seventh project. It's proof, built in layers, and each layer makes the next one believable.
First, a demo. A live link and a short recording show that the thing actually works.
Second, an architecture diagram, from the question to the answer. It shows you understand why it works.
Third, metrics. Hit rate from your eval set, cost per query, and p ninety-five latency.
Now the resume line can change. Action, scope, metric: built a RAG bot over twelve hundred documents, with its hit rate and its cost.
Those numbers are only examples. Yours must come from your own scripts.
Because the interviewer's next question is: how did you get eighty-seven percent?
A strong answer sounds like this: on sixty questions I wrote by hand, and the script is in the repo.
Small, honest numbers beat big, vague ones.
So pin three projects, not six, and make each one yours with your own data.
Then practise out loud: walk me through your project, in two minutes.
Remember: every number on your resume should be printed by a script in your repo.
That's the course. Go ship your proof.
